inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.

requested_area.areaDesc: Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

fields.description: NCM alert: convective clouds with light to moderate rain, possibly heavy at times, in some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior. In effect Saturday 22 Aug 2026, 13:30 to 21:00.
fields.headline: NCM alert: rain, heavy at times, possible in eastern, southern and western areas
fields.instruction: Take extra care when driving in rain and avoid standing water. Follow updates at https://alerts.example.ae.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and certainty to Possible because NCM describes light to moderate rain that may become heavy at times, and the source gives no time zone for 13:30–21:00. Please also check that the instruction, which is generic rain-safety advice not taken from the NCM text, fits your standard wording.

payload.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin on hazard (convective clouds with light to moderate rain, possibly heavy at times), times (Saturday 13:30 to 21:00), and areas (some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior). Severity Moderate and certainty Possible are consistent with the bulletin's 'possibility' wording and the CAP definitions. No unverified reports are included.

no_basis.concern: The sender is a demo stand-in identity, not one of the entities the UAE portal lists as authorised to send warnings. The register still treats it as the issuer, so this is a person's decision, not a register mismatch.

payload.summary: Within the issuing-authority mandate nothing is wrong. The sender is in the issuer register at level 1 with all areas and categories. The alert area and code (DEMO-ZONE / UAE-E-S-W) match the requested area drawn for event uae-rain-2026-08-22. Status Actual fits a real event on a live console. There are no active alerts from other authorities to overreach. This is an initial Alert, so no references are needed.

no_basis.concern: The TDRA-TS040 summary says messages should be limited to 1 page, but both languages run to several pages. This is a recorded gap (G6) and is below the 15-page maximum, so no objection is raised.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE page limit clause for cell broadcast messages

no_basis.concern: The first page names the hazard but gives no protective action for the public. The clauses shown set no requirement on action content, and this is a content matter for other reviewers.
no_basis.searched_for: first page must carry hazard and action requirement

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encodings are appropriate: English is GSM-7 and Arabic is UCS-2. English runs to 3 pages and Arabic to 5, both well under the 15-page maximum in 3GPP TS 23.041. The first page opens with the hazard ("NCM alert: convective clouds with light to moderate rain"), though the action is not stated in the text; that is a content matter rather than a delivery one. The page count is already covered by recorded gap G6, so I do not object to it again.

no_basis.concern: Arabic was produced by machine translation and needs human sign-off. This is a process point, not a meaning difference, and no shown clause sets a UAE rule on it.
no_basis.searched_for: UAE requirement for human review of machine-translated Arabic emergency alerts
